lessons.title: White-key note names

learn.title: Look at the black keys
learn.say: Black keys come in groups of 2 and groups of 3. Those groups are your map. C sits just LEFT of the group of 2. F sits just LEFT of the group of 3.
learn.tryText: Find a C. Play any C.
learn.hint: Look for a group of 2 black keys. C is the white key just to its left.

learn.title: Now F
learn.say: F is just left of the group of 3 black keys.
learn.hint: Find a group of 3 black keys. F is the white key just to its left.

learn.title: Going up
learn.say: In music, we name notes with the letters A to G. That's the whole musical alphabet: just 7 letters. Moving to the RIGHT, the letters go up in order. Watch and listen.

learn.title: Going down
learn.say: Moving to the LEFT, the letters go backward: G F E D C B A. Watch and listen.

learn.title: G wraps back to A
learn.say: After G, the alphabet starts over at A. The keys repeat, so the same letters show up again higher up.

learn.title: All seven names
learn.say: Every white key has one of those seven names. The pattern of black keys repeats, so the names repeat too.
learn.hint: D sits between the two black keys of the group of 2.

learn.title: One more
learn.say: Use the map: groups of 2 and 3 tell you where you are.
learn.hint: Count from F: F, then G is the next white key to the right.

lessons.title: White-key triads
lessons.practice: Build triads on different white keys: play one, skip one, play one, skip one, play one. Watch the chord name and numeral change.

learn.title: Skip a key, play a key
learn.say: Play a white key, skip the next one, and play the one after it. That jump is called a third. Stack two thirds (play, skip, play, skip, play) and you get a triad: a chord made of 3 notes. The bottom note is the root, the middle note is the 3rd, and the top note is the 5th. A triad is named after its root.

learn.title: Build your own triads
learn.say: Pick any white key as the root. Play it, skip one, play one (the 3rd), skip one, play one (the 5th), all at the same time.
learn.tryText: Build 4 triads on white keys, each starting on a different key.
learn.hint: Root, skip a white key, 3rd, skip a white key, 5th. Hold all three down together.

learn.title: Chords in a key
learn.say: Build a triad on every white key from C up to B and you get the chords in the key of C major: C, Dm, Em, F, G, Am and B°. The "m" means minor, a darker sound. B° (diminished) is the odd one out; it comes back later.

learn.title: Now F
learn.say: F is the root. Its 3rd is A and its 5th is C.
learn.hint: Find an F and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

learn.title: Now G
learn.say: G is the root. Its 3rd is B and its 5th is D.
learn.hint: Find a G and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

learn.title: A minor triad
learn.say: D is the root of D minor (Dm). Its 3rd is F and its 5th is A.
learn.hint: Find a D and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

learn.title: Same keys, new home
learn.say: A minor uses the same white keys as C major, but A is home. Its chords are Am, B°, C, Dm, Em, F and G.

learn.title: Home in A minor
learn.say: A is the root of A minor (Am). Its 3rd is C and its 5th is E.
learn.hint: Find an A and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

learn.title: One more
learn.say: E is the root of E minor (Em). Its 3rd is G and its 5th is B.
learn.hint: Find an E and build the triad up from there: skip a white key, play the next one, skip one, play one.

lessons.title: Roman numerals
lessons.practice: Play the chords of C major and watch their Roman numerals. Try a loop like I – IV – V – I, or I – V – vi – IV.

learn.title: Chords get numbers
learn.say: Each triad in a key gets a Roman numeral for the scale note it is built on. Capital numerals (I, IV, V) are major. Lower-case numerals (ii, iii, vi) are minor. In C major: I = C, ii = Dm, iii = Em, IV = F, V = G, vi = Am, vii° = B°.

learn.title: Play the IV
learn.say: IV is built on the 4th note of the scale: count C, D, E, F.
learn.tryText: Play the IV chord in C.
learn.hint: Count up four from C: C (I), D (ii), E (iii), F (IV). Find an F and build the triad up from there.

learn.title: Play the vi
learn.say: vi is built on the 6th note of the scale, and it is minor.
learn.tryText: Play the vi chord in C.
learn.hint: The 6th note of C major is A. Find an A and build the triad up from there.

learn.title: Numerals tell a story
learn.say: Songs move from chord to chord. That pattern is called a progression. I – V – vi – IV is one of the most-used progressions in pop music. Listen to it in C major.

learn.title: Same numerals, new key
learn.say: Now the same I – V – vi – IV in G major: G, D, Em, C. The chords are different, but the pattern is the same. In both keys, I is home: the progression keeps coming back to it.

learn.title: Play the progression
learn.say: Play each chord, let go, then play the next.
learn.tryText: Play I – V – vi – IV in C, one chord after another.
learn.hint: In C: I = C, V = G, vi = Am, IV = F.

learn.title: Another favorite
learn.say: I – vi – IV – V is the sound of 1950s doo-wop and lots of songs since.
learn.tryText: Play I – vi – IV – V in C, one chord after another.
learn.hint: In C: I = C, vi = Am, IV = F, V = G.

learn.title: Numerals in A minor
learn.say: In a minor key the numerals count from the minor home chord. In A minor: i = Am, ii° = B°, III = C, iv = Dm, v = Em, VI = F, VII = G. Same white keys as C major, but now Am is home.

learn.title: A minor progression
learn.say: i – VI – III – VII is a favorite in minor keys: dark, then lifting.
learn.tryText: Play i – VI – III – VII in A minor, one chord after another.
learn.hint: In A minor: i = Am, VI = F, III = C, VII = G.

lessons.title: Black keys and half steps
lessons.practice: Find every black piano key and say both of its names. Then walk up the keyboard in half steps, black and white.

learn.title: Two names for one piano key
learn.say: Black piano keys are named after the white piano keys on either side of them: the one to the left or the one to the right, depending on the music. Sharp (♯) means one piano key higher. Flat (♭) means one piano key lower. The black piano key between C and D is C♯, and it is also D♭. Same piano key, two names.

learn.title: Find F♯
learn.say: F♯ is one piano key above F: the first black key of the group of 3.
learn.hint: Find F, then play the black piano key just to its right.

learn.title: Find B♭
learn.say: B♭ is one piano key below B: the last black key of the group of 3.
learn.hint: Find B, then play the black piano key just to its left.

learn.title: The smallest step
learn.say: A half step is a move to the very next piano key, up or down, black or white, with no skipping. E to F and B to C are half steps too: there is no black key between them.

learn.title: A half step up
learn.say: Up means to the right.
learn.tryText: Play the piano key a half step up from E.
learn.hint: There is no black key right of E, so the next piano key up is F.

learn.title: A half step down
learn.say: Down means to the left.
learn.tryText: Play the piano key a half step down from D.
learn.hint: The very next piano key left of D is the black key C♯ (D♭).

lessons.title: Major and minor chords anywhere
lessons.practice: Pick any piano key as a root. Count up 4 half steps, then 3 more: major. Count 3, then 4: minor. Listen to the difference.

learn.title: Major 3rd = 4 half steps
learn.say: A 3rd is the distance from a chord's root up to its 3rd. Count it in half steps: every piano key, black and white. A major 3rd is 4 half steps. From C: C♯, D, D♯, E. So C up to E is a major 3rd.

learn.title: Play major 3rds
learn.say: Pick any piano key. Count up 4 half steps and play both keys together.
learn.tryText: Play a major 3rd (4 half steps) on two different piano keys.
learn.hint: Count 4 half steps up from your bottom note, black keys included.

learn.title: Minor 3rd = 3 half steps
learn.say: A minor 3rd is one half step smaller: 3 half steps. From C: C♯, D, E♭. So C up to E♭ is a minor 3rd.

learn.title: Play minor 3rds
learn.say: Pick any piano key. Count up 3 half steps and play both keys together.
learn.tryText: Play a minor 3rd (3 half steps) on two different piano keys.
learn.hint: Count 3 half steps up from your bottom note, black keys included.

learn.title: D and Dm
learn.say: When we name a chord, we shorten it. A major chord is written with just its root letter: D major is "D". A minor chord adds a small "m": D minor is "Dm". So "C" means C major, and "Am" means A minor.

learn.title: Bright and dark
learn.say: Major chords sound bright. Minor chords sound darker. Listen: D, then Dm. Then A, then Am.

learn.title: Major = 4 + 3
learn.say: Stack the two 3rds to build a chord. Major: a major 3rd on the bottom (4 half steps), then a minor 3rd on top (3 more). C major: C, up 4 to E, up 3 to G.

learn.title: Minor = 3 + 4
learn.say: Minor flips it: a minor 3rd on the bottom (3 half steps), then a major 3rd on top (4 more). C minor: C, up 3 to E♭, up 4 to G. Only the middle note moves.

learn.title: D
learn.say: Count from D: up 4 to F♯, up 3 to A.
learn.hint: D, up 4 half steps is F♯ (a black key), up 3 more is A.

learn.title: Cm
learn.say: Count from C: up 3 to E♭, up 4 to G.
learn.hint: C, up 3 half steps is E♭, up 4 more is G.

learn.title: A
learn.say: Count from A: up 4, then up 3.
learn.hint: A, up 4 is C♯, up 3 more is E.

learn.title: Fm
learn.say: Count from F: up 3, then up 4.
learn.hint: F, up 3 is A♭, up 4 more is C.

lessons.title: Inversions
lessons.practice: Play a chord, then move its bottom note up an octave: same chord, new inversion. Then try moving between chords with as little motion as you can.

learn.title: Same chord, new bottom
learn.say: An inversion is the same chord with a different note on the bottom. Root position: the root is lowest (C E G). 1st inversion: the 3rd is lowest (E G C). 2nd inversion: the 5th is lowest (G C E).

learn.title: C, 1st inversion
learn.say: Put E on the bottom.
learn.tryText: Play C major in 1st inversion (E on the bottom).
learn.hint: E, G, then the C above them.

learn.title: F, 2nd inversion
learn.say: Put the 5th (C) on the bottom.
learn.tryText: Play F major in 2nd inversion (C on the bottom).
learn.hint: C, then F and A above it.

learn.title: G, 1st inversion
learn.say: Put the 3rd (B) on the bottom.
learn.hint: B, D, then the G above them.

learn.title: Move as little as possible
learn.say: Good players move between chords with as little motion as they can. C to F: keep C, move E up to F and G up to A. C to G: keep G, move C down to B and E down to D.

learn.title: Your turn
learn.say: From C (C E G), the smoothest F keeps C on the bottom.
learn.tryText: Play F with C on the bottom (C, F, A).
learn.hint: Keep your thumb on C. Move the other two fingers up one white key each.
